delivery._note: 15 decided 2026-08-19; the old five-minute / 650-900 word goal is retired.

topic_priority.topic: Financial markets, banking, economy, Federal Reserve and SEC
Political policy with practical personal impact
Travel and airline or hotel loyalty programs

_junk_patterns_note: Case-insensitive regex, applied to headlines before scoring. Keep these narrow: dropping a real story is far worse than paying a fraction of a cent to score a dud. Built-in defaults live in src/normalize.js.

special_rules.health: State evidence stage: preclinical, observational, randomized trial, guideline, regulatory action, or unclear. Do not turn weak evidence into advice.
special_rules.finance: Explain market or policy significance; do not issue personalized buy or sell recommendations.
special_rules.politics: Prioritize enacted policy, court decisions, deadlines, taxes, benefits, schools, employment and direct practical effects over partisan commentary.
special_rules.local: Include only actionable or consequential local news, not routine filler.
special_rules.travel: Prioritize loyalty changes, major disruptions, routes, fees, status rules and material promotions.
special_rules.repeat_stories: Only repeat a continuing story when there is a substantive new development.

_schema_note: Keys below are the NEW profile structure (docs/PROFILE.md). geography_priority / topic_priority / delivery.max_stories are LEGACY, still read by the current src/score.js, and are deleted in the scoring-core phase. Everything else is keyed on enum values rather than English sentences, which is what lets score.js drop its CATEGORY_TO_TOPIC and GEO_TO_PREF translation tables.

sections.label: What Actually Matters Today
sections._note: Full field set. These are the developments most likely to change a decision — not the biggest headlines.

sections.label: Worth Knowing
sections._note: Fills the remainder up to target_stories. Headline + one-sentence why + link.

sections.label: Things I'm Watching
sections._note: Unresolved and forthcoming: proposed rules, pending launches, upcoming decisions. One line each.

relevance._note: relevance = 10 * (breadth + peak_gain * max(0, peak - breadth)) where breadth is the weighted mean and peak is max(peak_eligibility_i * dimension_i). peak_gain blends between the two: 0 is a plain weighted sum, 1 is pure max. peak_eligibility is what stops a dimension being GROUNDS rather than a MODIFIER — nothing is worth reading because it is merely new, or merely nearby.

financial_impact.description: Could move money you have, owe, earn, or plan to spend.

career_impact.description: Changes which jobs, skills, companies, or positioning make sense.

investment.description: Changes an investment thesis, valuation assumption, or industry structure.

decision_change.description: Could realistically change a decision you make. The sharpest test in the profile.

business_opportunity.description: A concrete entrepreneurial or small-business opening, with real economics.

property.description: Affects bookings, revenue, costs, risk, property value, or long-term viability of the rental property.

home_purchase.description: Affects mortgage financing, affordability, timing, or the target price range.

magnitude.description: Objective significance in the world. A modifier, never grounds — see the anti-anxiety rule.

geographic.description: Proximity. Your home town and county score highest here. A modifier, never grounds.

novelty.description: Genuinely new vs. a rehash. Can never by itself justify inclusion.

relevance._weights_note: Weights are RELATIVE and are normalized in src/score.js — they need not sum to 1. The nine dimensions from docs/PROFILE.md keep their stated percentages exactly; 'magnitude' is added on top (the profile lists it as primary objective #9 but omits it from the nine, and without it a genuinely enormous world event with no direct financial line scores near zero and never appears). Its low peak_eligibility keeps it a modifier, so catastrophe still cannot lead on size alone.

source_quality._note: Deterministic from the feed's source_class, never model-scored — it is a property of the outlet, known at retrieval. A cluster's effective quality is the BEST class among its members, so an aggregator that breaks a story is lifted when a primary source actually corroborates it. Floored at aggregator: if a feed reliably produces worse, delete the feed rather than pay to score it into irrelevance.
source_quality._model_floor_note: The model may demote a source at most this far, and may never promote one. Observations from the model; prices set by code.

allocation._note: Long-run targets, applied at SELECTION time as a bounded tie-break over a rolling window — never at scoring time, which would make a score depend on which batch it landed in. Bounded at +/-9 on a 0-100 scale: enough to reorder near-ties, never enough to promote a weak story over a strong one.
allocation._daily_ceiling_note: Max stories from one category in a single brief. Reader protection, not a target.
allocation._no_backfill_note: If a category has nothing worth sending today, send fewer stories. Never pad to hit a percentage.

quality_of_life._note: Outside the category percentages. Health, relationships, travel.

home_local._note: Geography home_region with a strong home-town signal (hyperlocal_terms below). Keeps local awareness alive on heavy national days.

property._note: Standing priority outside the geography percentages, capped at 1: with 2, property-area stories took 2 of the 5 lead slots in a labeled review. min stays 0 -- a trivial property-area story should never be manufactured into a slot.

heuristic_priors._note: Per-track priors for the $0 rule-based provider, moved out of code so the fallback is config-driven too.
heuristic_priors._hyperlocal_note: EXAMPLE. Place names that mean right where you live. A headline containing one scores 10 on the geographic dimension in rule-based mode.
heuristic_priors._property_note: EXAMPLE. Names that mean the rental area: the town, the county, the resort or attraction that drives demand, the road that reaches it.
heuristic_priors._category_note: track_category is only a FALLBACK. The heuristic derives category from which relevance dimension scored highest, because a track is a retrieval budget key, not a reason a story matters. Mapping property_local straight to a category made every property-area item 'quality_of_life' and swamped that bucket.

integrity._note: Framing penalties, applied MULTIPLICATIVELY. A flat point deduction is a different punishment at different score levels — 15 points is 17% of a 90 and 50% of a 30 — which penalizes weak stories harder than strong ones for the same offense. These are the profile's suppression list expressed as prices.
integrity._floor_note: Even a maximally flagged story keeps this fraction, so one bad framing call cannot zero out a genuinely important development.
